protein._shared.disclaimer: This email is general screening information from Lifeline Daily. It is not a diagnosis and not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always speak to a qualified clinician before making significant changes to your diet, particularly if you have a medical condition.
protein.protein_standard.subject: Your daily protein target from Lifeline Daily
protein.protein_standard.body:
Hi {{firstName}},

Based on what you told us, your daily protein target is about {{targetG}} g — that works out at roughly {{gPerKg}} g per kilogram of body weight.

{{rangeBlock}}

Spread it out. Aim for around {{perMeal}} g at each of your {{meals}} meals. Your body uses protein better in even portions across the day than in one large evening serving — and that matters more as you get older, not less.

As a rough guide: a palm-sized portion of chicken, fish or tofu is about 25–30 g; two eggs about 12 g; a pot of Greek yoghurt about 17 g; a cup of cooked lentils about 18 g.

{{sources}}

This is a target, not a prescription — and protein is only one part of the picture. If food or your weight is a source of worry, that is worth talking to a GP or a registered dietitian about.
protein.protein_renal.subject: Your Lifeline Daily protein check — please read
protein.protein_renal.body:
Hi {{firstName}},

You told us you have kidney disease or reduced kidney function, so our tool deliberately did not give you a protein target — and this email will not give you one either.

Here is why. In kidney disease, protein guidance runs in the opposite direction to general advice. National kidney guidelines recommend a reduced, closely supervised intake, set individually against your kidney function — and the right figure depends on your stage, whether you are on dialysis, and whether you also have diabetes. A general-population number could do real harm here.

So we are not going to guess. Please ask your kidney team or a renal dietitian for your personal target. That is the right answer for you, and it is not something a public calculator can safely replace.

If you were told you have reduced kidney function but have never had it followed up, that is worth raising at your next appointment.

diabetes.low.subject: Your Lifeline Daily diabetes screening result
diabetes.low.body:
Hi {{firstName}},

Your estimated 10-year risk of type 2 diabetes is {{riskPercent}}% — Low.

That's good news, and mostly comes down to habits worth keeping up. A re-check every 1–3 years (or sooner if your weight or health changes) is all that's usually needed.

{{crossChecks}}

Your BMI at the time of this check was {{bmi}}.
diabetes.moderate.subject: Your Lifeline Daily diabetes screening result
diabetes.moderate.body:
Hi {{firstName}},

Your estimated 10-year risk of type 2 diabetes is {{riskPercent}}% — Moderate.

Small, sustained changes now make a real difference at this stage. It's worth a lifestyle review, and asking your doctor about a blood test in the coming months.

{{crossChecks}}

Your BMI at the time of this check was {{bmi}}.
diabetes.high.subject: Your Lifeline Daily diabetes screening result — worth a check
diabetes.high.body:
Hi {{firstName}},

Your estimated 10-year risk of type 2 diabetes is {{riskPercent}}% — High.

This is the level at which health services recommend a check. Please arrange a blood test (fasting glucose or HbA1c) with your doctor soon.

{{crossChecks}}

Your BMI at the time of this check was {{bmi}}.
diabetes.veryhigh.subject: Your Lifeline Daily diabetes screening result — please read
diabetes.veryhigh.body:
Hi {{firstName}},

Your estimated 10-year risk of type 2 diabetes is {{riskPercent}}% — Very high.

Please don't be alarmed — it means action now is especially worthwhile. See your doctor soon to arrange a blood test and discuss next steps.

diabetes.symptomatic.subject: Your Lifeline Daily result — some symptoms worth checking
diabetes.symptomatic.body:
Hi {{firstName}},

You mentioned symptoms that can be caused by high blood sugar. Whatever your screening result, it's worth seeing a doctor soon for a simple blood test. This is not a diagnosis.

For reference, your estimated 10-year screening result was {{riskPercent}}% ({{riskBand}}).

{{crossChecks}}
diabetes.emergency.subject: Your Lifeline Daily result — please seek urgent care today
diabetes.emergency.body:
Hi {{firstName}},

You told us you feel very unwell right now — with symptoms such as vomiting, drowsiness, fast or deep breathing, or stomach pain. These can signal a serious problem with blood sugar.

Please seek a same-day medical assessment — urgent care or A&E. We haven't included a risk estimate, because getting checked comes first.

In an emergency, call your local emergency number now, for example 999 in the UK, 911 in the US and Canada, 112 in the EU and India, or 000 in Australia. In the UK you can also call NHS 111 for urgent advice.
